en.description:
Allez! Allez! is a cycling game for Apple Watch, all descent. You start at the top of a real col and go down the real road: every hairpin, every gradient, from map data of the mountain itself.

THE CONTROLS
• Roll the Digital Crown back to brake, forward to release. Grab too much and the wheels lock.
• Roll your wrist into the bend to lean. Lean too little and you run wide, over the white line, onto the gravel, and off.
• Tap left, right, left, right to pedal on the straights.

THE ROADS
• Col du Tourmalet, east side: the summit hairpins at 18%.
• Alpe d'Huez: bend 21 downwards.
• Sa Calobra: the tie-knot bend and the cliffs.
• Col du Galibier, north: high, fast and open.
• Mont Ventoux: off the bald summit and into the trees.
• Passo dello Stelvio: the first sixteen of the forty-eight.

Each descent is about five kilometres of real road, cut from the summit. The road drops away in front of you because the heights are the mountain's own.

THE DAY
Road paint, chevron boards, the devil with his pitchfork, crowds and campervans on the hairpins, the caravan, the photographer's moto, the helicopter, cows with bells. On the Pyrenean cols, the Basque wall.

THE TIMES
Every col has a Game Center leaderboard. Your best is kept on the Watch, and the team car tells you at each split whether you're up or down on it.

ON YOUR IPHONE
The companion app is the road book: each col from above with its hairpins marked, the elevation profile, your times and the Game Center boards, and the packs. Buy a pack on your iPhone and it's unlocked on your wrist.

Choose an aero, climbing or endurance bike. Turn the guide line on while you learn the line, off when you know it.

The six launch cols are free, with no ads, no account and nothing to sign up for. Four packs add four cols each for a single small purchase: the Pyrenees, the Alpes, the Dolomiti, and now España with the Angliru, Covadonga, Gamoniteiro and Masca. More packs follow.

The game is played on Apple Watch; the iPhone app is the road book and the shop. From the makers of Short Rounds and Long Glide.

Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors. Elevation: Copernicus EU-DEM.
en.releaseNotes:
The España pack: the Alto de l'Angliru at 24% with the brakes cooking, the Lagos de Covadonga from the lakes, the Alto del Gamoniteiro from the mast, and the nineteen hairpins of Masca, with a leaderboard each. The first Vuelta cols: the game now rides all three Grand Tours.

Also new: the fans at the roadside are people now. A puncture brings the neutral service car and two mechanics, one with a wheel and one to push you away. The brakes bite sooner at half a lever, the steepest pitches no longer drop out of sight, and the team car's messages sit on a plate you can read. The Gavia, the Giau and the Pordoi have lost some rises that had no business on a descent.
en.subtitle: Cycling descents on your wrist

versionHistory.releaseNotes: The Alpes pack: the Col d'Izoard through the Casse Déserte, the Col de la Madeleine, the Col de la Croix de Fer and the drop off the Col de Joux Plane into Morzine, with a leaderboard each. Hairpins on the Stelvio and everywhere else are drawn properly now.

The Dolomiti pack: the Passo di Gavia, the Mortirolo, the Passo Giau and the Pordoi down to Arabba, with a leaderboard each. Every col now has its own roadside: tricolori and pink balloons on the Giro's passes, the Basque wall in the Pyrenees, goats on Sa Calobra, Dutch Corner on the Alpe. A stop in play comes up as a road sign, the team car speaks the local language, and pedalling no longer runs away with the speed.

Unlocking a pack is more dependable. If the App Store can't be reached, the button now says so and tries again, rather than doing nothing. Purchases waiting on Ask to Buy approval are shown as waiting.
